samples.summary: The new off-slide refusal branch of `slides.elementCenter` has no test at any level
samples.evidence: `slides.elementCenter` gained a guard that refuses when the computed centre falls outside the canvas rect (bridge.ts, the `if (x < origin.left || x > origin.right || ...)` block), with a long rationale that it is what stops a manufactured 'clicking does nothing' defect. The sheet's equivalent guard is covered by `checkOffscreenRefusal` in verify-hunt-oracles.mjs, which asserts BOTH halves (an off-screen cell refuses with an 'off-screen' message, and a visible one still resolves and selects). The new `checkSlidesTargeting` only covers the unknown-id refusal (`no-such-element` / `Available:`); nothing nudges or scrolls an element off-slide and asserts the refusal fires, and nothing asserts the message content. So the branch could be inverted or deleted and every suite still passes. The unit test `slides-seed.test.ts` only asserts the SEED centres are inside 1920x1080 — that exercises the seed, not the guard.
searchedFor: grep 'off-slide' across repo (only bridge.ts and slides docs)
grep 'elementCenter' across repo (bridge.ts, page.tsx, verify-hunt-oracles.mjs, slides-seed*, docs)

samples.summary: "still overlaps, so a z-order change is visible" asserts only that SOME pair overlaps, so it passes even if the pair it is about is pulled apart
samples.evidence: The assertion is `SEED_FRAMES.some(a => SEED_FRAMES.some(b => ...intersects...))`. In the shipped seed both `badge`/`title` and `card`/`badge` intersect, so the test would still be green if `badge` were moved entirely clear of `card` — which is exactly the regression the comment says it exists to prevent ('no covered centres must not be achieved by pulling them apart'). A meaningful version would name the pair (or require every element to overlap at least one other) rather than a global existential.

samples.summary: "keeps every element inside the slide" only checks centres, and hardcodes 1920/1080 instead of the real SLIDE_WIDTH/SLIDE_HEIGHT
samples.evidence: The test name claims every element is inside the slide but the loop only asserts `centreOf(f)` is within (0,1920)x(0,1080). A seeded frame extending far past the slide edge (e.g. x:1800 w:1000) passes. It also hardcodes the bounds; `SLIDE_WIDTH = 1920` / `SLIDE_HEIGHT = 1080` live in packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:238-243, so if the slide size ever changed the test would keep asserting the old space while the harness scaled to the new one — the assertion silently stops describing the invariant it names.

samples.summary: `covers` is documented as edge-inclusive but no test exercises a boundary point
samples.evidence: slides-seed.ts:39 states the predicate is edge-inclusive ('a click on the edge still hits') and uses `>=`/`<=`. The only direct `covers` assertion (line 58) uses an interior point, and `coveredCentres` is exercised only with interior/clear centres. Flipping `>=` to `>` and `<=` to `<` would not fail any assertion in this file, so the documented edge semantics are untested.

samples.summary: The nudge oracle only asserts x changed, not that ArrowRight moved the element exactly +1 logical px
samples.evidence: `if (!moved || moved.x === originally.x)` in checkSlidesTargeting accepts any change at all, including a move in the wrong direction or by an arbitrary amount, and never checks `moved.y === originally.y`. The persona rubric (scripts/agent/charters-ui/slide-author.md) states as a measured FACT that arrow keys nudge by exactly one logical pixel and that round trips of N presses return exactly — the oracle that is supposed to protect that fact does not pin it, so the explorer would be told a magnitude the harness never verifies.

samples.summary: Slide navigation — the behavior the second brief leans on — is never exercised: `currentSlideIndex` is only checked at its initial value and `slides.elements` is never read on slide 2
samples.evidence: READER_EXPECTATIONS asserts `slides.currentSlideIndex === 1` and `slides.slideCount === 2` at rest, and `slides.selection` only for Array-ness. Nothing navigates to slide 2 and asserts the index becomes 2 or that `slides.elements` returns `[]` there, even though both the persona brief ('move between slides and watch what follows you') and the rubric ('slide 2 of the seed is empty, and reading `[]` there is correct') present those as measured facts. A `currentSlideIndex` frozen at 1, or `elements` still describing slide 1 after navigation, would pass every check in this diff.
searchedFor: read READER_EXPECTATIONS slides rows and checkReaderRegistry in verify-hunt-oracles.mjs

samples.summary: No test pins the slide-author rubric's measured traps, though the same file pins them for the sheet and doc rubrics
samples.evidence: `each rubric injects its OWN surface's constraints` asserts specific strings for sheet-author (canUndo, no-op, 'formatting toolbar IS mounted', 'DO NOTHING HERE') and doc-writer (per-keystroke, CLEAR THE SELECTION) precisely because a rubric fact is 'a claim with an expiry date'. The new slide-author rubric carries three equally load-bearing claims — you cannot drag, undo really works here, `Insert image` is unwired — and none is pinned; grep for 'slide-author' in scripts/agent finds only personas.json and the .md, never a test. Only the generic 'no rubric offers a visual ground' check touches it.
searchedFor: grep 'slide-author|cannot drag|slides.canUndo' in scripts/agent (hits only personas.json, slide-author.md, hunt-ui-tool.mjs)

samples.summary: Nothing in the unit lane ties SEED_FRAMES to the elements page.tsx actually seeds, so the geometry rule can be satisfied by a table the harness does not fully use
samples.evidence: slides-seed.test.ts asserts the rule over SEED_FRAMES only. page.tsx builds four elements via `frameOf(id)`, but an element added with an inline frame (or a SEED_FRAMES row that no element consumes) would leave the unit test green while the real seed violates the centre rule. The id/z-order pin exists only in verify-hunt-oracles.mjs's `ids !== "card,badge,title,body"` check, i.e. in the browser lane. Note also that the file header's justification ('a lane that is not run in CI') is inaccurate — scripts/verify-browser-lanes.mjs:72 runs `pnpm verify:hunt:oracles` inside the Docker browser job — which matters because the argument for the unit test's scope rests on it.

verdict.reason: The off-slide refusal branch in `slides.elementCenter` (bridge.ts:511-522) has no test at any level. checkSlidesTargeting (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:488-560) only asserts (a) seeded centres select themselves, (b) the unknown-id refusal names `Available:`, and (c) an ArrowRight nudge is observable — it never moves an element outside the canvas rect nor matches any refusal text against /off-slide/. The sheet's analogous guard IS covered, by checkOffscreenRefusal (400-456), which scrolls and asserts both the /off-screen/ refusal and that a still-visible cell resolves and selects; there is no slides equivalent. slides-seed.test.ts:31-41 only asserts the SEED frames' centres fall inside 1920x1080 — pure data geometry that never calls elementCenter or touches a canvas rect. No other consumer or test of the bridge exists: grepping `__WB_HUNT__`/`hunt/bridge` yields only page.tsx, hunt-ui-runner.mjs, verify-hunt-oracles.mjs and docs; scripts/agent/hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs only regex-scrapes reader names from bridge.ts, and hunt-ui-coverage.test.mjs's off-screen mention is about sheet.cellCenter journal entries. The branch (and its message) could be inverted or deleted with every suite passing — a shipped behaviour with zero meaningful coverage, major under the test-adequacy rubric.
